title.narrative: Second Costa Rica Disaster Risk Management Development Policy Loan with a CAT DDO

description.narrative: The PDO is to enhance the Government of Costa Rica's capacity to manage disaster risk resulting from the occurrence of natural and health related hazards and the impacts of climate change.

The development objective of the Second Costa Rica Disaster Risk Management Development Policy Loan with a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option (Cat DDO) for Costa Rica is to enhance the Government of Costa Rica's capacity to manage disaster risk resulting from the occurrence of natural and health related hazards and the impacts of climate change. The operation builds on the successful implementation and achievements of the first Cat DDO and reflects the ongoing policy dialogue and collaboration between the World Bank and the Government of Costa Rica on disaster risk management (DRM) and climate change adaptation. The operation is fully aligned with the government's DRM program and its efforts to address identified institutional, financial, and policy gaps. It is closely aligned with the priorities under the 2023-2026 national development and public investment plan; the 2020-2025 national risk management plan; and the 2018-2030 national climate change adaptation policy (PNACC). The operation is structured around two policy areas and four prior actions that support strategic actions aimed at increasing financial resilience against shocks; integrating climate, natural hazard, and gender-responsive climate risk reduction considerations into the government's investment planning processes; and promoting sustainable and risk-informed planning at the territorial level.

comment.narrative: A meeting will be held between the DCC, the CNE, and FONAFIFO to explore the possibility of incorporating information on emergency management and adaptation to climate events into the PAFT (Plan de Atención y Respuesta a Emergencias).

title.narrative: Percent increase in the share of female participants in local and municipal emergency committees who consider their participation has informed local programs and strategies for DRM and CCA

comment.narrative: End target modified through renewal. A first consultation with women involved in local organizations was designed and conducted to serve as a baseline. To accurately measure the indicator, a second round of data collection using the same tool is scheduled for the second semester of 2026.

title.narrative: Number of municipalities of the Sarapiqui Basin adopting the comprehensive basin management plan in their territorial management instruments

comment.narrative: The Sarapiqui River Basin Management Plan has been approved, and CODESOSA has been formalized as a prerequisite to advance to the local plans

title.narrative: Number of municipalities of the Sarapiqui Basin adopting the comprehensive basin management plan in their territorial management instruments

comment.narrative: The Sarapiqui River Basin Management Plan has been approved, and CODESOSA has been formalized as established in the Act. The regional plan needs to be adopted by municipalities. Currently, a six-month schedule is being prepared to carry out the presentation process of the Plan to targeted municipalities.

title.narrative: Number of municipal emergency committees trained to adopt the GBV prevention and management protocols for emergency situations

comment.narrative: There is a protocol in place to manage gender violence in emergency situations. This document will be expanded to address the issue from a prevention perspective, and efforts will be made to promote its inclusion in the Local Emergency Prevention and Response Plan of each Committee.

title.narrative: Percent increase in the share of female participants in local and municipal emergency committees who consider their participation has informed local programs and strategies for DRM and CCA

comment.narrative: Work is underway to design a survey for women involved in these spaces to understand their perception of how they have impacted their environment in relation to DRM (Disaster Risk Management) and CC (Climate Change) actions.

Number of Disaster Risk Financing Strategy Pillar action plans approved by the financial management coordination instance (ICO) and achievement of agreed implementation progress

comment.narrative: The Public Credit Directorate and the CNE, with the technical support of the World Bank, will implement a roadmap for the design, consultation and approval of the General Implementation Plan, which envisages the development of action plans under each of the four pillars. title.narrative: Percentage of financial preparedness plans and reconstruction/recovery investment plans that apply gender-differentiated impact and intersectional analysis

comment.narrative: The CNE has made progress in the disaggregation of data in the damage and loss assessment forms, for which it requests institutions to provide data disaggregated by sex, gender, ethnicity and disability conditions. Currently, 45 percent of post-disaster assessments, preparedness, reconstruction, and recovery investment plans apply intersectional and gender-differentiated impact analysis.

title.narrative: Percentage of financial preparedness plans and reconstruction/recovery investment plans that apply gender-differentiated impact and intersectional analysis

comment.narrative: The manual for project request and monitoring was revised to incorporate gender-differentiated and intersectional analysis, including disaggregated data and care-related categories, focused on reconstruction and recovery processes where gaps remained. Final editing of the documents is pending prior to submission for CNE Board approval.

title.narrative: Number of non-structural climate adaptation measures strengthened at the Sarapiqui Basin scale

comment.narrative: Target exceeded. Non-structural climate adaptation measures carried out by CODESOSA include: (i) joint work with the Instituto Nacional de la Mujer through a gender and climate change program; (ii) collaboration with UNED on gender-related environmental actions and a public awareness communication campaign; (iii) partnership with CCI Ambiental on a watershed-wide deforestation program, municipal cadastre, and aerial mapping; (iv) development of a Strategic Plan with EbaLAC identifying Ramsar zones; (v) collaboration with the Asociación Protectora de la Cuenca del Rio Sarapiqui on environmental crime reporting and citizen river observatories; (vi) reforestation, clean-up, and use of microorganisms through the Bandera Azul Ecológica program; (vii) reforestation of more than 60% of the watershed; (viii) economic valuation of ecosystem services with the Instituto Panamericano de Sostenibilidad; and (ix) work with the Dirección de Aguas on transparency and communication.

title.narrative: Number of municipalities that incorporate the climate adaptation variable into their operational, strategic, or human development planning instruments approved by the Municipal Councils.

comment.narrative: The DCC will conduct a consultation with local governments to identify which ones have plans that include climate adaptation measures.

title.narrative: Number of municipalities that incorporate the climate adaptation variable into their operational, strategic, or human development planning instruments approved by the Municipal Councils.

comment.narrative: Indicator name modified through renewal. As of the current reporting period, 31 municipalities have approved planning instruments, up from the baseline of 22, against an end target of 50. In addition, 18 municipalities reported instruments pending approval, and 8 municipalities are in the final stages of preparation and adoption.
